name: Video Depth Anything
plain: Video Depth Anything (ByteDance): depth of a whole clip via `model.video(frames)` (a plain call treats frames as independent), consistent over time; relative and metric. Apache-2.0 code and weights (Small only).
summary: Video Depth Anything (Chen et al., CVPR 2025): temporally consistent depth of long videos from the Depth Anything V2 encoder and a DPT head with temporal attention, run in overlapping 32-frame windows; relative (Small) and metric (Metric Small) checkpoints.

papers.title: Video Depth Anything: Consistent Depth Estimation for Super-Long Videos

licence_notes: Only the Small checkpoints (relative and metric) are Apache-2.0; the Base and Large checkpoints are CC-BY-NC-4.0 and not included.
The metric model is trained on Virtual KITTI 2 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) and IRS per the upstream README (a note only).
limitations: `model.video(frames)` runs one video in time order (each window attends over time and is aligned to the previous one); calling the model with an image or a batch runs each image as a one-frame video.
Every video runs at least one 32-frame window (shorter videos are padded with copies of their last frame): one image costs about as much as 32 frames in the temporal head.
The whole video's depth is kept on the device as float32 (L x H x W); split very long videos.

Video Depth Anything Small at 40 frames of 480 × 640 in FP16 uses 1,231 MiB portable and 1,297 MiB kernels on an RTX 5060 Ti, with warm medians of 458.1 and 375.8 ms. Depth matches bitwise on this clip and three labeled TUM clips within each mode.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant`, `affine_invariant_log` (log depth) and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.42 % and p99 <= 0.55 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `inverse_depth`).
